To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a consensus-sequence synthetic pentatriccopeptide repeat (PPRs) protein has been produced, crystallized and its structure determined, revealing the structural basis of PPR protein function and providing a basis for future design.

we designed a synthetic PPR motif based on a consensus-sequence and that it has high thermal stability and can form long arrays of PPR repeats, thus providing a suitable backbone for bespoke RNA-binding protein designs with potential for high specificity.

a consensus-sequence synthetic pentatriclopeptide repeat (PPr) protein can form long, soluble, helical tracts, with high thermal stability, that are structurally and functionally similar to natural PPR proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of synthetic proteins with RNA-binding properties, which can be used to control gene expression.
the design and characterization of synthetic proteins, and the development of methods for the de novo design and production of bespoke proteins for a wide range of biotechnological applications.
the design of bespoke proteins for the manipulation of RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPR proteins can be successfully designed and that the structure and function can be controlled by rational design.
PPR proteins have the potential for biotechnological use, but that there are many hurdles to overcome before they can be routinely used.
the design and structural characterization has been achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to protein design based on the use of consensus sequence information.
this study provides a framework to understand the structural basis of PPR protein function, and the basis of PPR-RNA recognition, which is the foundation of our future design efforts.
we designed and produced the first synthetic PPR protein, and determined its crystal structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple consensus-sequence synthetic protein can be designed and expressed in a form that allows structural analysis.
a consensus sequence can be used to design a synthetic PPR with a well defined structure and high stability, and that this can be used to generate a long tract of PPR repeats.
synthetic PPR proteins can be produced in high quantities and with high stability.
